steps.label: Receive
steps.title: Begin with what was actually said.
steps.text: Reserve an owner- and character-scoped turn. Keep the current message and recent dialogue distinct from stored summaries and inferred state.
steps.example: “My interview moved to Monday. Please skip the pep talk today.”
steps.detail: Originals preserve wording, speaker, timestamp and source ID.

steps.label: Recall
steps.title: Retrieve context, with its sources.
steps.text: Semantic facts answer what is currently known. Episodic summaries recall what happened together. Their originals remain available for checking. Core notes, open loops, recent exchanges and character state complete the bounded context.
steps.example: Current fact: interview on Monday. Episode: a previous practice session. Preference: quiet support today.
steps.detail: Pinned boundaries and updated facts precede matching memories; optional follow-up lookup can recover sources.

steps.label: Respond
steps.title: Answer the person, with continuity.
steps.text: Your model receives the assembled context, persona and response guidance. It returns a reply, cited memory proposals and optional attunement/appraisal fields.
steps.example: “Monday, got it. Want to leave interview stuff alone for a bit?”
steps.detail: Attunement describes the current cue and response intention; it is not a permanent personality fact.

steps.label: Commit
steps.title: One turn, several kinds of memory.
steps.text: Validate structure and source quotes, then atomically store the conversation and permitted fact changes. Keep superseded revisions separate from current knowledge. Deliver the committed reply through the host.
steps.example: Friday → Monday updates the current fact. The original Friday message still belongs to history.
steps.detail: Automatic / review / off policies govern memory proposals. Provenance checks do not prove semantic truth.

steps.label: Consolidate
steps.title: Turn history into useful continuity.
steps.text: When consolidation is due, a host or configured worker produces a cited episode and refreshed core. Optional notes, links and vectors make these records easier to retrieve.
steps.example: One practice session becomes an episode; the current interview date stays in the core notebook.
steps.detail: Consolidation derives records; it does not erase the original conversation.

steps.label: Continue
steps.title: Two loops feed the next reply.
steps.text: Memory preserves events and changing knowledge. Character emotion follows a separate bounded state update with time decay. Both return to the next context.
steps.example: Remember the reschedule without treating a stressful afternoon as a permanent trait.
steps.detail: Character emotion is fictional writing state. It is separate from user memory and from attunement evaluation.

views.label: Retrieval & recency
views.description: Original evidence, archive memories and open threads use distinct rankings.

steps.label: Find
steps.title: Search originals and derived memory.
steps.text: Originals use raw contextual vectors, separate note vectors and lexical matches. Keep top 32 raw, 16 note and 60 lexical candidates. Facts and episodes have their own archive search.
steps.example: A semantically similar message can be found even when it uses different words.
steps.detail: Vectors are optional; layered search additionally has a bounded CJK substring channel.

steps.label: Fuse
steps.title: Preserve evidence; rank archive memories.
steps.text: Evidence uses RRF: sum 1/(40 + rank), with bounded one-hop links. Archive facts and episodes use 0.6 relevance + 0.25 exp(-age_days/45) + 0.15 importance/10.
steps.detail: Archive age uses event/reinforcement time for facts and source-span end for episodes. No age penalty on original evidence.

steps.label: Prioritize
steps.title: Recency belongs to the follow-up queue.
steps.text: Open facts marked followup=ask are ranked by importance, arousal, age since update and event-date proximity. The queue selects up to 12 items. It does not initiate an unsolicited message.
steps.example: An important interview tomorrow can outrank a similarly important but older loose end.
steps.detail: Age is measured in days. An absent event date contributes no urgency bonus.

steps.label: Assemble
steps.title: Selection is more than a single score.
steps.text: Pinned boundaries, corrections and recent turns also enter context. Core notes and matched episodes retain source IDs. Whole-entry budgets bound the payload; optional follow-up tools expand related originals.
steps.example: A recent correction can be included even if an older statement had a higher similarity rank.
steps.detail: Observation-date filtering applies to original recall. Fact validity/event dates use a separate temporal lookup.

views.label: Consolidation
views.description: Compress the context. Keep the evidence.

steps.label: Trigger
steps.title: A durable backlog makes work repeatable.
steps.text: New SDK characters consolidate after 20 pending exchanges, 12k characters, 300 seconds idle, or a knowledge invalidation. Busy chat retains the newest 10 exchanges; idle flush handles short conversations.
steps.example: A running worker checks the durable backlog; reaching an idle threshold does not wake a stopped process.
steps.detail: Thresholds are configurable. A running host or worker must act on due work.

steps.label: Write
steps.title: Let one writer own the summary.
steps.text: SDK defaults enable configured background writers; MCP defaults use host authoring. Each batch evolves grounded notes and writes episodes, a cited user notebook and optional separate character core.
steps.example: Episode: the rehearsal and reschedule. Notebook: current commitments and grounded response preferences.
steps.detail: Host and background summary modes are mutually exclusive. Character self-core is optional and kept separate.

steps.label: Commit
steps.title: Citations survive compression.
steps.text: Validate the supplied original IDs and snapshot/version before committing. Append the episode, replace the current core, record processed sources and preserve the originals. Reject a stale write if facts changed.
steps.example: A summary can be traced back to the exact original message, not just another summary.
steps.detail: Citation validation establishes provenance, not independent factual verification.

steps.label: Refresh
steps.title: Corrections close the cycle.
steps.text: Fact changes invalidate current core and affected cited documents. With no source turn, invalidation is broader. Search indexes update with records; changed text or notes invalidate vectors for re-indexing.
steps.example: Monday replaces Friday in current knowledge. The old transcript remains historical evidence with a knowledge-update marker.
steps.detail: Embeddings need a configured provider. Corrections are not silent rewrites of original dialogue.

views.label: Emotion & continuity
views.description: A character has continuity, not a mood reset.

steps.label: Interpret
steps.title: Read the moment without making it a trait.
steps.text: A short attunement record captures the cue, intent and uncertainty. An optional appraisal proposes a character emotion and relationship-axis changes. These are separate from factual user memory.
steps.example: “They sound tired; offer a little space” describes this turn, not the user’s personality.
steps.detail: Appraisals are model proposals. They are not psychological measurements.

steps.label: Decay
steps.title: Time softens mood and tension differently.
steps.text: PAD moves toward baseline with a 12-hour half-life. Tension halves over 72 hours. Warmth above 0.6 × familiarity cools after 7 absent days, with a 35-day half-life.
steps.example: After 12 hours, half of a PAD deviation remains; tension retains about 89%.
steps.detail: Small seeded daily character weather is applied once per UTC day during preparation.

steps.label: Update
steps.title: Warmth is earned; boundaries remain current.
steps.text: Appraisal intensity pulls PAD toward an emotion target. Relationship deltas saturate, repeated positive warmth is reduced, trust loss is asymmetric and each axis has a 0.12 daily movement budget.
steps.example: Romance cannot grow without opt-in or until familiarity exceeds 0.2 after this turn’s familiarity update.
steps.detail: Axes: trust, warmth, familiarity, tension, romance. Band hysteresis avoids flip-flopping.

steps.label: Carry
steps.title: Let the next answer inherit the state.
steps.text: Persist the bounded state and turn interpretation separately. The next context can include a relationship note, recent attunement records and linked user feedback. Current corrections and boundaries take priority.
steps.example: A slightly guarded character can still offer respectful support and follow the user’s request for space.
steps.detail: The chart below isolates decay; it omits new appraisals, daily weather and absence cooling.
